images.source: Flat faceted paper fields under a wide sky that shifts from the deeper blue of late afternoon at the right to the pale first light of morning at the upper left. One satin ribbon in a gradient from Alliance Blue to Ribbon Cyan arcs across the whole sky from the afternoon side into the morning side, where a faceted paper blossom is just opening at its end: an afternoon’s work arriving at the start of a day. Calm sky in the upper left quarter. Portrait, about 8:9, safe to crop to 4:5. Palette only: Partner Navy #121B2A, Alliance Blue #1B56FF, Ribbon Cyan #00D5FF, Daylight #F4F7FB and the shades between them. Nature built from satin ribbon and flat paper facets. Light from the upper left, soft navy-tinted shadows falling down and to the right. No text or letters, no people, no hands, no robots, no brains, no circuit boards, no sparkles, no glow, no purple or pink, no regional or cultural motifs, no real places or landmarks.

notes: Deliberate exception to the site's sample clock moment (Manila 9:41 am, London 1:41 am): the UK strip shows a November afternoon in Manila (4:41 pm, London 8:41 am) so the clocks show the headline, and the caption says so. The FAQ answer to 'Where is your team?' uses Brand DNA facts (seven or eight hours ahead; we work as part of the partner’s team) in the Australian page’s pattern, so it doesn’t repeat the headline. Clutch gives a UK figure only for web design in our sources, so the UK table has one row and claims nothing else. Every promise on the page is Brand DNA wording: the five price promises are verbatim from 'Our honest pricing promise' (confirm each is true before launch), the price card line is the Brand DNA's embedded-developers line, and the FAQ answers are the Brand DNA's 'Questions buyers will ask'. Header marks no nav item. One Primary in the hero and one in the closing band. Every number carries a Source key and a dated source line in its own section. Review 2026-11-03: full name in the price card; the goal links read “See how we …” instead of “Explore …”. The hero lead, the clock-strip title and the first answer no longer repeat the headline. Lead image pass 2026-11-03: section-specific images replace backgrounds that repeated across pages.
